ai_summary: Great Britain is currently recording an aggregate wind output of 12.0 GW, with estimated Scottish wind output contributing 1.0 GW, representing 9.9% of installed Scottish wind capacity. Scotland’s generation mix demonstrates exceptional regional performance, maintaining a Scottish carbon intensity of 0 gCO2/kWh versus 58 gCO2/kWh GB-wide. However, grid transmission bottlenecks continue to limit the full delivery of low-carbon electricity across borders. So far today, 204 MWh of Scottish generation has been curtailed through Balancing Mechanism bids, incurring a constraint cost of about £6,641. To replace this trapped renewable volume closer to demand centres, an estimated 38,741 m3 of gas was burned elsewhere on the system, resulting in an additional 71 tonnes of CO2 emissions. Extrapolating today’s constraint spend indicates an estimated total yearly cost of curtailment of approximately £2 million. Spread across national demand, this constraint burden increases everybody's invoice in the UK by approximately £0.01/MWh. These metrics underline the persistent environmental and operational costs of network congestion, where zero-emission Scottish generation is restricted and replaced by fossil fuels while adding balancing expenses to consumer bills.
